gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: College makes every curve match its straight stems, with big counters in a tall lowercase, while Noto Sans Mandaic turns curvy. Big and short is where it earns its keep.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-mende-ki: Diagonals that match the stems, curves too, give College a dynamic, authoritative stance. Noto Sans Mende Kikakui lets daylight through every curve and stands tall, a lighter, plainer voice beside it.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-multani: Dynamic and authoritative, College keeps its curves as sturdy as its stems, with big counters in a tall lowercase. Noto Sans Multani, plain sans with lofty x-height, carries paragraphs smoothly.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Smooth and unflickering: College has no stroke contrast to catch the eye, just big counters in a tall lowercase. Give College the large sizes and let Noto Sans Myanmar handle the text.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham leaves wide gaps in the e and looks bold from tall bodies, while College glows like neon tubing. Glassy uniform strokes over a plain sans make the pair instantly recognizable.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Noto Sans Old Italic sits tight between x-height and cap height, keeping its curve endings well apart. And College, with rounds and stems in one weight, does display best while the sans-serif body handles detail.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-nort: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and tall, with outward-pointing terminals. College, with stylus-steady strokes, earns its keep big and short, where its wide counters can really show off.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-perm: Drafting-pen steadiness runs through College, every curve matching its stems around big counters in a tall lowercase. Noto Sans Old Permic, rounded and open with near-capital lowercase, feels friendlier beside it.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-pers: Drawn-wire strokes, big counters: College looks dynamic and authoritative, with a tall lowercase. And Noto Sans Old Persian lets open counters breathe, so paragraphs of its plain sans read cleanly.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-palmyren: Straight-edged and constant: College holds every stroke steady, with big counters in a tall lowercase, over Noto Sans Palmyrene. That plain sans partner stops curves short and keeps ascenders compressed.
